title: A group says which of its pieces are not following it
goal: A group can now tell its contents how to line up, and any one piece can disagree. There is no way to see the disagreements: you have to click every piece in turn to find out which ones have a rule of their own. The group should say so where the setting is.
notes: From the placement audit 2026-09-03. The data is already there: Layer.placement is non-nil exactly on the pieces that override. PlacementInspector.contentRows is where it goes.
acceptance: With a group selected, the Layout section names the pieces inside it that have their own rule
Clicking one of those names selects that piece
A group where nothing disagrees says nothing extra rather than showing an empty list

log.note: Adversarial review before building: the mock had no list at all, this came out of the placement audit. Two things were cut. (1) A 'put them all back to following' button: it is one undoable stroke that would wipe rules the user set on purpose, from a section they came to for something else. (2) Showing every override in the whole subtree: what a grandchild says is an argument with ITS group, and listing it here would name a piece the group's own setting has no power over. Kept: direct children only, the rule each one carries, and a click that goes there.
Core: Layer.contentsWithTheirOwnPlacement + PlacementOverride in PhotonzCore/LayerPlacement.swift, top-most first to read like the Layers list. Seven tests in LayerPlacementTests.

UI: PlacementInspector.exceptions, at the bottom of contentRows, under the caption it is the exception to. Count line, then up to six rows (name, what it does, chevron), then 'and N more'. Empty list shows nothing. Click calls selectLayer(id, inGroup: group), which is what reveals it in the Layers list.

Verified on the probe with Scripts/playtest/placement-exceptions-walk.json (Screen Recording granted, so real captures): nothing overriding shows nothing extra, one override reads 'One layer has a rule of its own', two read '2 layers have rules of their own', and the pick lands the selection on the listed piece inside the frame (log step 31: selection Rectangle, insideGroup Frame). New probe-only action pickFirstOwnRule makes the click reachable from a walk.

Review after building: two pieces both named Rectangle read identically, which is the app's layer naming, filed as its own task. Hover highlight is not photographable from a walk. Nothing here touches Current: the whole Layout section sits behind next-placement.
